question: Which wallets or anchors let users cash Stellar USDC or XLM out to local bank, card, or mobile-money rails, and how should a builder integrate last-mile cash-out?

golden.answer:
A grounded answer derives its named examples and status claims from the current LumenLoop corpus, then dates the roster so it is not presented as permanent. As of 2026-07-11, a live mobile-money partner search returned 13 matches, with Zeam Money and Boss Pay among the first results.

The dated example is illustrative: a later grounded answer should report what the same source basis supports at its own observation time while preserving the stable distinctions above.
keyFacts: Makes the as-of date visible for every changeable roster, status, version, or measurement.
Stellar lacks local-bank, debit-card, M-Pesa, Wave, Orange Money, MoMo, or USSD rails.
Those come from anchors, wallets, payment processors, or local partners.
Checks provider assets, countries, KYC, fees, limits, settlement times, and API/SEP fit.
avoid: Do NOT claim a mobile-money corridor is supported without current provider evidence.
Do NOT imply Stellar can directly push funds to mobile-money or bank rails without an off-chain partner.
Do NOT answer only at the corridor-selection/cost-structure level; this question owns the last-mile payout-rail integration, including failed-payout remediation.
Do NOT claim the observed live result set is a complete or permanent roster; explicitly historical facts remain historical.
golden.notes:
2026-06-29: Sharpened to own last-mile payout-rail integration — promoted consumer-wallet-vs-builder-API split and failed-payout remediation to should_have, added a must_avoid against answering only at the corridor-selection level (that lane is owned by q-crp-anchors-by-corridor). MoneyGram USDC cash-out and HoneyCoin mobile-money lead unchanged; country/mobile-money support stays monthly-freshness.
Also good if the answer: Separates consumer wallet availability (a user can cash out) from builder/API availability (a separate partner/API contract, KYB, webhooks, SLAs, reconciliation). | Treats failed/partial/reversed last-mile payout (wrong number, agent-network outage, USSD failure, dormant mobile-money account) as a remediation/support requirement the builder must design for. | Maps SEP-24/6 withdrawal (and SEP-31 for cross-border) as the on-chain side that hands off to the off-chain payout partner, not the payout itself.
Golden cites: Dated provider/anchor docs or directory entries for any named cash-out option.

corroboration.claim: As of 2026-08-29, official architecture docs assign local bank, card, mobile-money, and USSD payout rails to anchors and partners, not to the Stellar network itself.

evidence.note: Exact quote: anchors are ‘on and off-ramps that connect the Stellar network to traditional financial rails.’

Dated web sweep query `Stellar mobile money off-ramp USSD partner anchor`: top primary results were Stellar Ramps (`on and off ramps provided by anchors`), Stellar cross-border payments (`local partners` provide payout), and SeevCash (`Ramp API` disburses GHS to Mobile Money). No primary result assigned a local payout rail to the network itself.
